# Izuki (Nova Izuki)

> Izuki is a free, open-source AI assistant for Windows 10 and 11. Say "Hey Nova" and talk naturally: Izuki sees your screen, answers out loud, and uses your mouse and keyboard to get things done. It also works from your phone and on your TV.

Izuki is free to use. It runs on free AI keys from Google Gemini, Groq (including Meta's Llama models), OpenRouter, Mistral or NVIDIA, or on a model running on your own PC with Ollama. Keys stay on the user's PC.

## What it does

- Hands-free voice ("Hey Nova") or hold Ctrl + Windows + Space to talk
- Sees the screen and answers questions about it ("what does this error mean?")
- Does tasks on the PC: opens apps, searches, clicks, types, scrolls, fills in forms, checking each step worked
- Jarvis mode: presses buttons and types into boxes straight through Windows, so the user's own mouse stays free
- Works beside you: if you use the mouse while it works, it waits, then carries on
- Teacher mode for quizzes and homework: explains with an on-screen pen, never submits for you
- Paste step-by-step directions from another AI and Izuki carries them out on screen
- Alarms, reminders and day planning on the PC and phone
- Send it pictures in the chat, Discord or Telegram
- PC Boost: notices a slow PC and speeds it up (old temp files, hogging background updaters)
- A status screen with live system health and one-tap fixes
- Controls Roku, Samsung, LG, Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV, and can say what's on the TV
- 30+ voices and real 3D characters, including comic-book and flat-art styles
- A browser extension for exact clicks on web pages
- Safety: Esc stops everything, it never types passwords or card numbers, and asks before sending
